name: Agniveer Army GD
fullName: Indian Army Agniveer (General Duty) – Online Common Entrance Examination
nameHi: भारतीय सेना अग्निवीर (जनरल ड्यूटी) सामान्य प्रवेश परीक्षा
approxCandidates: Several lakh registrations per cycle (approx.; the Army does not publish exact figures)
eligibility: Class 10 with 45% aggregate and 33% in each subject. Age 17½–21 per the scheme; reports say the upper limit was raised to 22 for the 2026 registration cycle, so check the current notification

notification.summary: Registration for recruiting year 2027 ran from 13 February to about 10 April 2026, and the online CEE was held from 1 to 16 June 2026. ARO-wise CEE results were published on 12 July 2026, and recruitment rallies (physical tests and medicals) followed from late July 2026. The next cycle's registration is expected around February–March 2027 on joinindianarmy.nic.in.

pattern.stage: Phase I – Online Common Entrance Examination (CEE), Agniveer GD
pattern.notes: The section split (15/15/15/5) and the marking of +2 / −0.5 follow the widely reported GD pattern since negative marking was introduced in 2023. Secondary sources disagree on the marking, so check it against the current Army notification. The pass mark has been reported as 35 out of 100. Phase II is the recruitment rally (physical fitness and measurement tests, adaptability test, documents and medical). The bank holds 60 items: GK 18, Science 18, Maths 18, Reasoning 6.

trendAnalysis.summary: The paper is at Class 10 level and mostly easy to moderate. General Science (basic Physics, Chemistry and Biology facts and units) and General Knowledge (Indian history, geography, polity, defence and static GK) are the most scoring areas. Mathematics covers arithmetic, mensuration and simple algebra or geometry, and it was reported as the toughest section in the June 2026 CEE. Reasoning is short: series, coding, analogy and directions. Because of negative marking, accuracy matters more than attempting everything, and difficulty has been stable since the CEE format began in 2022–23.

resources.notes: The Army does not publish CEE question papers or answer keys. joinindianarmy.nic.in carries the notification, syllabus, practice or mock-test links and ARO-wise results, and papers circulating online are memory-based.

questions.question: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was Prime Minister from 1947 to 1964. Dr Rajendra Prasad was the first President.

questions.question: Who is popularly known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title for integrating more than 560 princely states into India.

questions.question: Bhagat Singh was executed in 1931 along with:
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in Lahore on 23 March 1931, now observed as Shaheed Diwas.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan (about 3.42 lakh km²) is the largest by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: The river Ganga originates from:
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi rises at Gaumukh, the snout of the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand, and becomes the Ganga at Devprayag after meeting the Alaknanda.

questions.question: The Siachen Glacier lies in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Siachen lies in the eastern Karakoram. Indian troops hold it, and it is called the highest battlefield in the world.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: There were originally 10 (42nd Amendment, 1976). The 86th Amendment (2002) added an 11th, on education of children aged 6–14.

questions.question: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Chief Justice of India under Article 124(2).

questions.question: The Constitution of India came into force on:
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.question: Except for the one-rupee note and coins, currency notes in India are issued by the:
questions.explanation: The RBI issues currency notes. The Government of India (Ministry of Finance) issues the one-rupee note and coins.

questions.question: How many players of one team are on the field in a hockey match?
questions.explanation: Each field hockey team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.question: The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest:
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award. The Ashoka Chakra is the peacetime equivalent and the Bharat Ratna the highest civilian award.

questions.question: The headquarters of the Indian Army's Southern Command is located at:
questions.explanation: Southern Command is at Pune. Northern Command is at Udhampur, Central at Lucknow and Eastern at Kolkata.

questions.question: Army Day is celebrated in India on:
questions.explanation: 15 January marks the day in 1949 when Gen. K. M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief. 8 October is Air Force Day, 4 December Navy Day and 7 December Armed Forces Flag Day.

questions.question: What is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The Bengal tiger is the national animal. The peacock is the national bird.

questions.question: The book 'The Discovery of India' was written by:
questions.explanation: Nehru wrote it in Ahmednagar Fort prison in 1944, and it was published in 1946.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: The newton is the SI unit of force (1 N = 1 kg·m/s²). The joule measures energy, the watt power and the pascal pressure.

questions.question: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an erect, diminished image and a wider field of view.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity on the Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² near the Earth's surface.

questions.question: Electric current is measured with a/an:
questions.explanation: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current. A voltmeter measures potential difference.

questions.question: A body covers 100 m in 20 seconds. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed = distance/time = 100/20 = 5 m/s.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.question: Which gas is the most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere and oxygen about 21%.

questions.question: Lemon juice is sour mainly because it contains:
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits contain citric acid. Acetic acid is found in vinegar and lactic acid in curd.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of carbon?
questions.explanation: Carbon has 6 protons. Its common isotope has mass number 12.

questions.question: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature.

questions.question: A solution with a pH value less than 7 is:
questions.explanation: pH below 7 is acidic, exactly 7 is neutral and above 7 is basic (alkaline).

questions.question: Which cell organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.question: Deficiency of vitamin C causes:
questions.explanation: Scurvy (bleeding gums) is caused by lack of vitamin C. Rickets comes from vitamin D deficiency, night blindness from vitamin A and beriberi from vitamin B1.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles.

questions.question: Which blood components help in the clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) help form clots at the site of injury.

questions.question: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ overall. The liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.question: Deficiency of iodine in the diet causes:
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormones, and its deficiency enlarges the thyroid (goitre).

questions.question: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 91 = 7 × 13, 87 = 3 × 29 and 51 = 3 × 17, but 97 has no divisors other than 1 and itself.

questions.question: What is the LCM of 8, 12 and 18?

questions.explanation: √144 = 12 and √81 = 9, so the sum is 21.

When a number is increased by 20%, it becomes 360. The number is:
An article bought for ₹500 is sold for ₹450. The result is:
questions.explanation: Loss = ₹50, which is 50/500 × 100 = 10% loss.

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹660, a shopkeeper gains 10%. The cost price of the article is:
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their sum is 56. The larger number is:
questions.explanation: 56 × 4/7 = 32 (the smaller is 24).

What amount will ₹1,000 become in 2 years at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually?
A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, they will finish it in:
questions.explanation: 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6, so together they take 6 days.

What is the perimeter of a square of side 12 cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48 cm. Note that 144 cm² would be its area.

questions.question: What is the area of a circle of radius 7 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area = πr² = 22/7 × 49 = 154 cm². Note that 44 cm is the circumference.

questions.question: If 3x − 7 = 11, then x equals:
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. The largest angle is:
questions.explanation: The angles sum to 180°, so the largest is 180 × 4/9 = 80°.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 5, 10, 20, 40, ?
questions.explanation: Each term doubles, so 40 × 2 = 80.

questions.question: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so J + 5 = O.

questions.question: If CAT = 24 (C = 3, A = 1, T = 20), then DOG = ?
Find the odd one out:
questions.explanation: Rifle, pistol and carbine are firearms, while a helmet is protective gear.

questions.question: Eye : See :: Ear : ?
questions.explanation: The eye is used to see and the ear is used to hear.

questions.question: Ravi is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise and then turns 180°. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: A 90° clockwise turn from North faces East, and a 180° turn from East faces West.
